1) Torsion-based anti-TICT argument is suggestive but not decisive because only delta-dihedral is provided (E31, E21). A near-zero delta (0.017°; E21/E31) can occur if the chromophore is already twisted in S0 and stays twisted in S1; without absolute dihedral angles (S0 and S1), “no twisting” does not imply “no TICT”.
2) The ICT support is moderate rather than strong: redistribution is “medium” (E36/E35) and permanent dipole change is only ~0.404 D (E62), while “rigidity proxy high” and “relaxation proxy low” (E39, E37) mainly say geometry doesn’t change much, not that the emissive state is CT.
3) The aTB excited-state electronic observables raise a plausibility red flag: S1 oscillator strength is 0.0 and transition electric dipole is extremely small (E61, E60). If these correspond to the emissive state, radiative emission would be unlikely; if not, then the analysis needs an explicit statement that the computed S1 may be dark and emission may originate from another state (or aggregate-state physics not captured here).
4) ESIPT is appropriately downweighted by structure priors (no donor sites / no H-bond geometry; motif/profile indicates no proton-transfer prerequisites), but that structural argument wasn’t explicitly anchored to evidence_ids in the mechanism narrative. E57 also indicates compact-prior neighbor reliability is low and label entropy high, so “ESIPT present in compact neighbors” shouldn’t be over-interpreted.
5) “Solid-only emission at 587 nm” (E71–E73) is not sufficient to claim AIE behavior or to tie aggregation to any specific mechanism; missing solution and aggregate PL prevents confirming enhancement vs quenching, shift direction, and whether the observed band is monomer-like or aggregate/excimer-like.
